note: What one unit is told to do: a path of points on the ground plane, or nothing at all. Every point after the first states each of its coordinates either as a step from the point before it or afresh, and a run of flags read first says which.

bits.name: hasTeleportToken
bits.note: Set where a token sits beside the unit.

bits.name: pointCount
bits.note: How many points the path holds, and never fewer than one in anything observed. What a payload carrying zero holds after this byte is unrecorded, so a reader meeting one has met something this document does not describe.

fields.name: path
unit
fields.note: The unit the path belongs to.

fields.name: flags

bits.name: xIsStep
bits.note: Set where this point states its first coordinate as a step.

bits.name: zIsStep
bits.note: Set where this point states its second coordinate as a step.

fields.note: One pair for each point after the first, in the order the points follow. Pairs run on from the low bits of the first byte, and the run reaches to the byte holding the last pair. The bits past it are clear.

fields.name: firstX
fields.note: The first point, along one ground axis, in the units spec/movement.md gives.

fields.name: firstZ
fields.note: The first point, along the other.

fields.name: xStep
fields.note: Added to the first coordinate of the point before, as that point resolved.

fields.name: xWhole
fields.note: The first coordinate, stated without reference to the point before.

fields.name: zStep
fields.note: Added to the second coordinate of the point before, as that point resolved.

fields.name: zWhole
fields.note: The second coordinate, stated without reference to the point before.
Everything the movement carries beyond its first byte.
